title: Where Harry Edison's style came from
summary: They discuss Edison's individual style and St. Louis background, and the many trumpeters from St. Louis.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Now where did Harry's style come from? I mean what was his sort of inspiration?
DANCE: More like Roy. CLAYTON: Yes.
I don't know.
It doesn't seem to fit exactly, does it?
To fit who?
It doesn't seem to fit into the categories, you know, where you could say that Dizzy was sounding like Roy Eldridge and ......
No, it doesn't sound like anybody.
It doesn't really, no.
Not to me. It sounds just like Harry.
Yes.
I don't know where he got his style from. He had been playing in St. Louis in the Jeter-Pillars band out of St. Louis.
Oh, that's right, yes.

And I heard there was another trumpet player out there that he liked and his name was Harry something else. Basie knew him. In fact, Basie and this other trumpet player named Harry Smith had played together on an old road show somewhere. They were room mates. But I don't know whether that's where Harry got
his style or not.
Well there were a lot of trumpet players in St. Louis weren't there?
Yes. St. Louis was another hot spot for musicians.
Yes, yes.
Do you remember Jimmy Blanton?
Yes. But I mean there was Shorty Baker and (Clark Terry) and all those ......
Yes.
